title: Tactical card combat
summary: A combat model where players choose from a constrained hand or deck and resolve actions against a shared tactical state.

designQuestions: Is resolution turn-based, simultaneous, or real-time?
What information is public or hidden?
How are cost, range, target, timing, and counterplay communicated?
How does the hand refresh preserve agency?
designKnowledge.accessibility: Communicate active player, target, range, cost, and outcome using text and shape as well as color; support touch-sized selection and confirmation.

technicalPatterns.name: Resolve validated intent
technicalPatterns.guidance: The client submits an action ID and target intent. The server validates phase, ownership, cost, target, and current board state before applying a deterministic result.

technicalPatterns.name: Separate definition from runtime state
technicalPatterns.guidance: Keep immutable card definitions separate from each player's deck, hand, cooldown, and match state; validate definitions at load time.

technicalPatterns.name: Record ordered outcomes
technicalPatterns.guidance: Represent multi-effect actions as an explicit ordered resolution so clients present the same result and tests can assert it.

dependencies.rationale: The family record describes decision quality and multiplayer rules.
A collection may supply a deck, while owned cards and match legality remain separate concerns.
Match actions and outcomes must be validated by the declared server authority.

failureModes.description: The client and server interpret a selected target or range differently.
failureModes.mitigation: Use shared definitions and server-side legality checks; show invalid targets before submission where possible.

failureModes.description: Clients animate chained effects in a different order than the server result.
failureModes.mitigation: Replicate an ordered resolution record and test late or repeated delivery.

scenarios.action: Submit valid and invalid cards, targets, phases, costs, stale versions, and replays.
scenarios.expected: Only a legal current action changes authoritative match state once.

scenarios.action: Complete a turn using a touch-sized viewport without hover or keyboard-only instructions.
scenarios.expected: The player can identify phase, legal targets, cost, and result.

acceptanceCriteria: Card definitions and runtime ownership are separate.
Illegal and repeated actions are rejected by the server.
The choice and result remain legible to all clients.

considerations: Bound hand and effect counts by the actual design; profile the largest resolution sequence on mobile.
Avoid rebuilding every card view for each small state update.

evidence.description: Action contract, authority, failure modes, and repeatable mobile and multiplayer scenarios are specified.

assumptions: This record does not select turn timing, deck size, balance, or monetization.
A complete game needs its own rules, content, and playtest evidence.
